CHIEF COMPLAINT
Acne on the face.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Kayla Ward is a 18-year-old female presenting with acne located on the face that started approximately two years ago and is present most days. She denies associated symptoms including itching, bleeding, or pain. The patient reports that acne is not significantly present on the chest or back. She has been using Persa-Gel and washing regularly, which has been somewhat helpful. Mother reports that the biggest flare occurred when the patient started school sports in the fall due to sweating. The patient denies flares with her menstrual cycle and reports having a regular period for approximately two years. Today is reported as a good day for acne. Mother notes that despite the patient's good compliance with facial care regimen, the acne has not improved as much as desired.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies itching, bleeding, or pain associated with acne. No other systemic symptoms reported.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
None reported.

MEDICATIONS
Persa-Gel (benzoyl peroxide)
Elf Super Clarity Cleanser
Toner

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives with parents and sister. Household pets include a dog, bird, and bunnies. Currently in 7th grade. Participates in basketball, volleyball, and tap dancing. Wears sunscreen SPF 30 in the summer. Current skincare routine: Morning - washes face with water and washcloth, occasionally uses Elf cleanser if face feels greasy. Evening - uses Elf Super Clarity Cleanser, followed by toner and Persa-Gel.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Full body examination performed except under underwear and bra. Multiple benign nevi on trunk and extremities. Scattered skin-colored papules. Open and closed comedones noted. Erythematous papules on face, primarily on forehead with some on central cheeks and chin. Chest and back relatively spared. Remainder of examination normal.

RESULTS
Diagnosis: Mild to moderate acne, mostly comedonal with small inflammatory component. Multiple benign nevi with no worrisome features.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Acne: Start topical therapy. Morning routine: wash face with mild cleanser, apply noncomedogenic moisturizer with SPF 30 or higher. Evening routine: wash face with mild cleanser, allow to dry, apply adapalene 0.1% cream in thin layer to affected areas starting a few nights per week and gradually increasing to nightly use. Can substitute with over-the-counter retinoid gel if adapalene is expensive or not covered by insurance. Follow with Clean and Clear Persa-Gel in thin layer and noncomedogenic moisturizer. Counsel patient regarding potential side effects including sensitivity, dryness, and irritation; emphasize need for sunscreen when outdoors. Benign nevi: Reassure patient that all nevi appear normal with no worrisome features. Follow up in 6 months to assess progress. Patient to call office with any questions or concerns before next visit.
